Line and paragraph counts help with poetry, code, and list formatting.
Characters-without-spaces is what many publishers and translators actually bill by.

faqs.a: Words are split on whitespace: any run of spaces, tabs, or line breaks separates two words. So 'hello, world' counts as two words, and multiple spaces between words do not create phantom words.
A paragraph is a block of text separated by at least one blank line. Three lines with no blank lines between them count as one paragraph, even though they are three lines.
Line breaks count as characters, because they are stored in the text. The 'characters without spaces' figure excludes all whitespace: spaces, tabs, and line breaks.
faqs.q: Do line breaks count as characters?

faqs.a: Yes. The counter splits sentences on '.', '!', '?', and the ellipsis character. Abbreviations like 'Dr.' can inflate the count slightly - that is normal for automatic counters.
Probably. Different tools define words and paragraphs slightly differently - for example, whether hyphenated words count as one or two. Small differences of a few percent are normal.
faqs.q: Why does another counter give a slightly different number?

faqs.a: Yes. It runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you paste is uploaded, stored, or seen by anyone else.

line-counter.formula:
lines = text split on '\n' -> count
non-empty lines = lines where trim() is not empty -> count
paragraphs = text split on blank lines (2+ newlines) -> non-empty chunks -> count
words = trim(text) split on whitespace -> count
characters = text.length (includes line breaks)
characters without spaces = text with all whitespace removed -> length
sentences = text split on . ! ? ... -> non-empty chunks -> count
average words per line = words / lines

Example: 'Hello world\n\nThis is a test'
  lines: 3 ('Hello world', '', 'This is a test')
  non-empty lines: 2
  paragraphs: 2
  words: 2 + 4 = 6
  characters: 11 + 0 + 14 + 2 newlines = 27
  characters without spaces: 25 - 4 spaces = 21
howTo: Paste or type your text into the input box.
All eight statistics update live: lines, non-empty lines, paragraphs, words, sentences, characters, characters without spaces, and average words per line.
Use the Copy button to copy the full statistics summary to your clipboard.
Clear the box to start over with new text.
keyFacts: A line is everything up to the next line break; an empty line still counts as a line.
Non-empty lines ignore lines that contain only spaces or tabs.
A paragraph is a block of text separated from the next by at least one blank line.
Words are separated by whitespace: spaces, tabs, and line breaks.
Character counts include line breaks; the without-spaces count strips all whitespace first.
Sentences are split on '.', '!', '?', and the ellipsis character.
line-counter.keywords: count lines, line counter, word counter, character counter, paragraph counter, text statistics
limitations: Word and sentence definitions are approximations; hyphenated words and abbreviations can shift counts.
It counts text structure, not quality - a high word count does not mean good writing.
Right-to-left and mixed-script text is counted the same way; some scripts have no word spaces at all.
Extremely large pastes (millions of characters) may briefly slow the page.

line-counter.workedExample:
Input text:
Hello world

This is a test

Step by step:
1. Lines: split on line breaks -> 'Hello world', '', 'This is a test' = 3 lines.
2. Non-empty lines: the middle line is empty -> 2.
3. Paragraphs: split on the blank line -> 'Hello world' and 'This is a test' = 2.
4. Words: 'Hello world' = 2, 'This is a test' = 4 -> 6 total.
5. Characters: 11 + 0 + 14 = 25, plus 2 line breaks = 27.
6. Characters without spaces: 25 - 4 spaces = 21.
7. Sentences: no sentence-ending punctuation -> 0.
8. Average words per line: 6 / 3 = 2.
